display.title: Episode 414: The Storyteller, Chapter 9 (The Final Chapter)
display.summary_short: A family's Hakochainik letter, the final chapter of The Storyteller, Shema with a seven-year-old yeshiva boy, and Mitzvah Time on when and where we say the Shema.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in early Shevat 5750. The mailbox brings a letter from a girl in Far Rockaway whose whole family marches around the supper table with spoons and teapots during the Hakochainik march, and Uncle Yossi notes the show has been on the air for eight years; then everyone joins the march. Story time brings the final chapter of The Storyteller. Before finishing, a seven-year-old yeshiva boy who loves saying the Twelve Pesukim says the Shema in Studio 604. Then the answers arrive: the Baal Shem Tov had told Yitzchak that the day someone came and told him this very story would be the day his past was forgiven. The wealthy merchant reveals that he is that Yitzchak, thanks Hashem in tears, and shares his wealth with Rabbi Yehuda, fulfilling the Baal Shem Tov's blessing; Rabbi Yehuda and his wife resolve to give tzedakah generously. After tzedakah, Uncle Yossi launches a phone quiz and teaches Mitzvah Time: the Shema is said evening and morning, comes from Devarim chapter 6, and is followed by 'Baruch Shem.' The show ends with the Tzivos Hashem Children's Expo and candle time.
display.lesson: Hashem's ways are wondrous: help comes at the right moment, and it is never too late to return to Him.
